description: Task: write a Python function solve(nums1, nums2) that returns the median of all values of the two lists taken together, as a float. Each argument is a list of integers in non-decreasing order with 0 to 1000 elements and values between -1000000 and 1000000 inclusive, and at least one of the two lists is non-empty. The median of an odd number of values is the middle one and of an even number the mean of the two middle ones: for nums1 = [1, 3] and nums2 = [2] the answer is 2.0, and for nums1 = [1, 2] and nums2 = [3, 4] it is 2.5.

Task: write a Python function solve(nums1, nums2) that returns the median of all values of the two lists taken together, as a float. Each argument is a list of integers in non-decreasing order with 0 to 1000 elements and values between -1000000 and 1000000 inclusive, and at least one of the two lists is non-empty. The median of an odd number of values is the middle one and of an even number the mean of the two middle ones: for nums1 = [1, 3] and nums2 = [2] the answer is 2.0, and for nums1 = [1, 2] and nums2 = [3, 4] it is 2.5.

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

catalogue.mechanism: merge the two lists with two indices up to the middle
binary search a cut of the shorter list so that the left halves hold the smaller values
merge through heapq (heapq.merge or pushes and pops) up to the middle
